types.name: Attorney (lawyer)
types.plain_description: A lawyer licensed by the State Bar of California. A corporation or LLC must have one to go to court (outside small claims), for example to foreclose a mechanics lien. A lawyer is also the person to ask for advice on contracts, claims and disputes.

when_required.situation: Your company is a corporation or LLC and needs to file or answer a lawsuit in any court other than small claims (a lien foreclosure, payment bond, stop payment notice or contract suit).
when_required.legal_basis: CSLB guidance: 'If you are a corporation or limited liability company, you cannot represent yourself in court other than small claims court and must obtain the services of an attorney.' (CSLB 2026 Law Book, Section III, printed p. 50; the court rule behind it is not cited there)

when_required.situation: Someone outside your company gives you legal advice, chooses or writes legal terms for you, or represents you: only an active State Bar licensee may practice law in California. (A registered legal document assistant may prepare documents you choose yourself, at your direction, but may not give legal advice.)
when_required.legal_basis: Business and Professions Code 6125 (unauthorized practice of law); 6400 and following (legal document assistants)
when_required.note: Not read: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov answered with a Cloudflare bot challenge, which was not bypassed.

not_required_when.situation: Small claims court: both sides represent themselves and neither may be represented by an attorney. You cannot foreclose a mechanics lien in small claims. CSLB cites a limit of up to $12,500 (CCP 116.221), but that higher limit is for a claim brought by an individual; a corporation or LLC is held to the lower limit in CCP 116.220 ($5,000 in the text printed in CSLB's 2022 Law Book; the current amount was not read). Check the current limit with the court.
not_required_when.legal_basis: CSLB 2026 Law Book, Section III, printed p. 48 (cites CCP 116.221); CCP 116.220(a)(1) and 116.221 as printed in the appendix of CSLB's 2022 Law Book
not_required_when.note: CCP 116.221 applies to 'an action brought by a natural person'; CCP 116.220(a)(1) sets the general limit (read in the 2022 Law Book appendix, https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf). Later amendments to the dollar amounts were not checked because leginfo.legislature.ca.gov is behind a bot challenge.

not_required_when.situation: A partner or sole proprietor may represent themselves in court and is not required to have an attorney.
not_required_when.legal_basis: CSLB 2026 Law Book, Section III, printed p. 50

optional_when.situation: A recorded mechanics lien is enforced by a lawsuit to foreclose it, which must be filed within 90 days after the lien is recorded (the deadline printed in the notice every lien claim carries). It cannot be brought in small claims court. A lawyer is legally required for it only if your company is a corporation or LLC (see above); a sole proprietor or partner may file it themselves, but talking to a lawyer well before the deadline is advisable.
optional_when.legal_basis: Civil Code 8416(a)(8) (the notice: suit 'no later than 90 days after the date the mechanics lien is recorded'; the deadline itself is in Civil Code 8460, which was not read); CSLB 2026 Law Book, Section III, printed pp. 48 and 50 (no lien foreclosure in small claims; who must use a lawyer)
optional_when.note: Statute text as printed in the appendix of CSLB's 2022 Law Book (fetched 2026-11-26); later amendments were not checked because leginfo.legislature.ca.gov is behind a bot challenge. The small claims and self-representation statements were read in the CSLB 2026 Law Book (https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/2026/2026_CSLB_Law_Book.pdf) on 2026-11-26.

types.name: Notary public
types.plain_description: A person commissioned by the California Secretary of State to confirm who is signing a document and notarize the signature. A notary does not check whether the document is legally correct and is not your lawyer.

when_required.situation: After your bonding company (surety) pays a claim on your CSLB bond, or someone holds an unpaid court judgment against you, you may settle by an agreement (an 'accord') instead of paying in full (or, for a judgment, filing a bond). If you settle by an accord, the copy you file with CSLB to avoid or lift a license suspension must be notarized.
A document has to be recorded with the county recorder and the recorder requires the signature to be acknowledged before a notary (many documents affecting title).
when_required.note: Not read: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov answered with a Cloudflare bot challenge, which was not bypassed.

types.name: Professional engineer (civil, structural, geotechnical, electrical, mechanical and others)
types.plain_description: An engineer licensed by the Board for Professional Engineers, Land Surveyors, and Geologists (BPELSG). An engineer designs, stamps and signs work that California law or the Cal/OSHA safety orders say must come from an engineer, for example sloping or benching for an excavation deeper than 20 feet.

when_required.situation: Sloping or benching an excavation deeper than 20 feet: the design must come from a registered professional engineer.
when_required.legal_basis: 8 CCR 1541.1, Appendix B, note 3 ('Sloping or benching for excavations greater than 20 feet deep shall be designed by a registered professional engineer')

when_required.situation: Any sloping, benching, support, shield or other protective system that does not follow the standard options (the Appendix tables, the manufacturer's tabulated data or other tabulated data) must be approved, and for sloping and benching stamped and signed, by a registered professional engineer. A written copy naming the engineer must be kept at the jobsite while it is built.
when_required.legal_basis: 8 CCR 1541.1(b)(4) and (c)(4); federal equivalent 29 CFR 1926.652(b)(4) and (c)(4)
when_required.note: Federal text read through the official eCFR API: https://www.ecfr.gov/api/renderer/v1/content/enhanced/current/title-29?part=1926&section=1926.652

when_required.situation: When shoring or shield material or equipment is damaged and the competent person cannot confirm it can still carry the loads safely, it must be taken out of service and evaluated and approved by a registered professional engineer before it is used again.

Anyone may prepare plans for certain small wood-frame buildings: wood-frame single-family homes and wood-frame buildings of up to four dwelling units (not clusters that add up to more than four units on a lot), of not more than two stories and basement; their wood-frame garages; and wood-frame agricultural and ranch buildings (unless the building official finds an undue risk). If any part of such a building departs from conventional wood-frame requirements, the building official must require that part's plans or calculations to be prepared by or under a licensed architect or registered engineer, stamped and signed. Either one may do it.
when_required.note: Statute text as printed in the appendix of CSLB's 2022 Law Book (fetched 2026-11-26); later amendments were not checked because leginfo.legislature.ca.gov is behind a bot challenge.

when_required.situation: Electrical or mechanical design: a licensed contractor may design electrical or mechanical systems for work it will install and supervise within its classification. That exemption does not cover designing work someone else will install; a contractor's engineering services beyond it must be done by or under the responsible charge of a registered electrical or mechanical engineer.
when_required.note: Statute text as printed in the appendix of CSLB's 2022 Law Book (fetched 2026-11-26); later amendments were not checked because leginfo.legislature.ca.gov is behind a bot challenge.

when_required.situation: Design services beyond Section 5537 or the contractor's own license scope must be performed by or under a licensed architect or professional or civil engineer.
when_required.note: Statute text as printed in the appendix of CSLB's 2022 Law Book (fetched 2026-11-26); later amendments were not checked because leginfo.legislature.ca.gov is behind a bot challenge.

when_required.situation: Where the building code requires special inspections, a statement of special inspections prepared by the registered design professional (the architect or engineer responsible for the design) is needed before the permit is issued.
when_required.note: The building code text was not read; ask the building department what it requires.

types.name: Licensed architect
types.plain_description: An architect licensed by the California Architects Board. California law lets anyone prepare plans only for certain small wood-frame buildings (Business and Professions Code 5537); plans for other buildings generally come from a licensed architect or engineer.

when_required.situation: The exemption in B&P 5537 covers plans for: wood-frame single-family homes and wood-frame buildings of up to four dwelling units, of not more than two stories and basement; their wood-frame garages and similar structures; and wood-frame agricultural and ranch buildings (unless the building official finds an undue risk). If an exempt building departs from conventional framing, the building official requires that part to be prepared and stamped by a licensed architect or a registered engineer; either one may do it.
when_required.note: Statute text as printed in the appendix of CSLB's 2022 Law Book (fetched 2026-11-26); later amendments were not checked because leginfo.legislature.ca.gov is behind a bot challenge.

when_required.situation: Plans for buildings outside the B&P 5537 exemption must generally be prepared by a licensed architect or by a registered engineer working within the branch of their license; for most buildings either one can do it. Some building types have their own rules.

when_required.note: Statute text as printed in the appendix of CSLB's 2022 Law Book (fetched 2026-11-26); later amendments were not checked because leginfo.legislature.ca.gov is behind a bot challenge.

types.name: Qualified SWPPP Developer (QSD) and Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP)
types.plain_description: Stormwater professionals under the State Water Board's Construction General Permit. Generally a QSD writes the stormwater pollution prevention plan (SWPPP) and a QSP carries it out on site, including inspections and sampling. The permit text could not be read when TradeComply last checked; confirm with the Water Board.

when_required.situation: Construction that disturbs one acre or more of land (or less than one acre when it is part of a larger common plan of development or sale that will disturb one acre or more) needs stormwater permit coverage: an individual permit or coverage under a general permit. Five acres or more is 'construction activity'; one to under five acres is 'small construction activity', which does not include routine maintenance to keep the original line, grade or purpose of a facility. In California that coverage is normally the State Water Board's Construction General Permit, which is where the QSD and QSP requirement comes from (next item).

types.name: Cal/OSHA-certified asbestos consultant (CAC) or site surveillance technician (CSST)
types.plain_description: A person certified by Cal/OSHA (the Division of Occupational Safety and Health, DOSH) who is paid to provide asbestos health and safety services: building inspections, abatement design, contract administration, sampling, management plans and clearance air monitoring. A site surveillance technician (CSST) works on site as a consultant's (CAC's) independent representative.

when_required.situation: Anyone who contracts to provide professional asbestos health and safety services (building inspections, abatement project design, contract administration, sampling, management plans, clearance air monitoring) as an asbestos consultant, or who works as a site surveillance technician, must be certified by DOSH.
A building owner or operator that hires asbestos consulting or site surveillance work must contract with a DOSH-certified person.

Cal/OSHA's rules require DOSH certification for anyone who performs services as an asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician, and no employer may use one who cannot show it. Cal/OSHA's definition and the DOSH search page describe this as work on 100 square feet or more of asbestos-containing construction material, but the statute (B&P 7180 and 7181) sets no size limit, so do not treat a smaller job as exempt.
when_required.legal_basis: 8 CCR 341.15(a); 8 CCR 1529(q)(1), (q)(4); DOSH certification search page
when_required.note: 8 CCR 1529(q) read at https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/1529.html and the DOSH page at https://www.dir.ca.gov/databases/doshcaccsst/caccsst_query_1.html, both on 2026-11-26. The DOSH page says 'more than 100 square feet'; 1529(q)(1) says '100 square feet or more'.

when_required.situation: Before asbestos-related work begins, the owner of a commercial or industrial building, the employer or the contractor doing or contracting for the work must make a good-faith effort to find out whether asbestos is present; for a building built before 1978 the contractor or employer first asks the owner. This law does not itself say who does the survey; if you pay someone to do it, B&P 7180 and 7180.5 require a DOSH-certified consultant.
when_required.note: Statute text as printed in the appendix of CSLB's 2022 Law Book (fetched 2026-11-26); later amendments were not checked because leginfo.legislature.ca.gov is behind a bot challenge.

not_required_when.situation: A licensed contractor or registered asbestos abatement contractor may take no more than 12 bulk samples in a residential dwelling for its own bid, its own employees' exposure, or to judge its own abatement contract, if the people sampling are AHERA-certified building inspectors. The contractor may not provide professional health and safety services, risk assessments or (unless otherwise permitted) clearance air monitoring.

A preliminary site assessment or other building inspection whose main purpose is not finding asbestos and judging whether it needs abatement (for example a general property condition inspection) is not the asbestos consulting that needs certification. It does not replace the asbestos survey before demolition or renovation.

types.plain_description: The local government office that issues building permits, checks plans and does inspections. Inside a city it is usually the city; in unincorporated areas it is the county.

types.name: Special inspector / deputy inspector (approved by the building department)
types.plain_description: An inspector approved or registered by the building department to watch certain work continuously, such as structural concrete, steel, welding or masonry. In Los Angeles these are LADBS Registered Deputy Inspectors.

when_required.situation: City of Los Angeles: builders who need continuous inspection use LADBS-certified Deputy Inspectors; LADBS says that without a Deputy Inspector holding the correct certifications, approval for the related work may not be given.

types.name: Competent person (Cal/OSHA)
types.plain_description: Someone you designate, usually your own trained foreman or superintendent, who can spot existing and predictable hazards and has authority to fix them right away. It is not a state license, so there is no public directory.

when_required.situation: Some safety orders require a competent person: for example, when shoring or shield material is damaged, a competent person must examine it before it is reused (8 CCR 1541.1(d)(3)). A competent person is one who can identify existing and predictable hazards and is authorized to take prompt corrective measures.
